title: Energy at the same spin
hook: Change moment of inertia and predict rotational kinetic energy.
misconception: rotational kinetic energy stays fixed when moment of inertia doubles.
objective: Apply K_rot = ½Iω² to compare rotational kinetic energy when moment of inertia changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a rigid object rotating at fixed angular speed, K_rot = ½Iω². When moment of inertia doubles, rotational kinetic energy becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model K_rot = ½Iω²; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a rigid object rotating at fixed angular speed, with a nonzero initial result. If moment of inertia triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on rotational kinetic energy?
recall.why: Apply K_rot = ½Iω² under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
